reference.title: Dumbbell Lunge
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step forward and lower, exhale as you push back to standing.
breathing.cadence: About 1.6 s step and lower, short pause, about 1.7 s push back

prescription.tempo: Controlled step, 1-2 s down, push back in about 1 s
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, then walking lunges with dumbbells. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, palms facing in.
Take a long step forward and land heel first; the dumbbells hang straight down.
Breathe in and lower the back knee toward the floor; back heel up, chest tall.
Breathe out and push off the front foot to step back to standing.
Stand tall and reset; alternate legs.

mistakes.fix: Keep the front knee over the 2nd-3rd toe; shorten the range if needed.
Lengthen the step and keep the weight in the front heel.
Lower under control and stop just above the floor.
Let the arms hang long and still at the sides; shoulders down.

kinematics.norm: Front knee about over the front foot at the bottom (common guideline); about one leg length was suggested as optimal in the split squat (Song 2023)
About 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Lowers to just above the floor, about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Upright to slightly forward; more lean shifts work to the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008)
Hang straight down at the sides, clear of the thighs and the floor (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: López-de-Celis, Labata-Lezaun et al. 2023, effect of load distribution on trunk muscle activity with lunge exercises in amateur athletes (Healthcare 11(6):916)
Hip, knee and ankle joint moments in the single-legged squat, forward lunge and reverse lunge (J Athl Train; PMC4641539)
Farrokhi et al. 2008, trunk position influences lead-leg kinematics, kinetics and muscle activity in the forward lunge (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 38:403-409)
Song et al. 2023, effects of step lengths on lower-extremity biomechanics during the split squat (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1277493)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: start with the reverse lunge, which loads the knee less (PMC4641539).
Balance concerns: one dumbbell in the hand away from a support, the other hand on the support.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors brake the step and drive the push back.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors brake the step and drive the push back.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; hip moments were greater in the forward lunge than in the reverse lunge (PMC4641539), and more so with the trunk inclined forward (Farrokhi 2008).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; hip moments were greater in the forward lunge than in the reverse lunge (PMC4641539), and more so with the trunk inclined forward (Farrokhi 2008).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the toes on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the toes on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall. With the load split evenly in both hands, trunk muscle activity stayed more symmetrical than with one dumbbell (López-de-Celis 2023).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright; erector spinae side-to-side differences seen with one dumbbell were absent with a bilateral load (López-de-Celis 2023).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright; erector spinae side-to-side differences seen with one dumbbell were absent with a bilateral load (López-de-Celis 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders level and stop the dumbbells pulling the shoulder blades down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders level and stop the dumbbells pulling the shoulder blades down (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Stand tall, dumbbells at the sides
